newsitem.title: FRANCE: FIGURE SKATING-RUSSIAN SKATING FACES UNCERTAIN FUTURE.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-RUSSIAN SKATING FACES UNCERTAIN FUTURE.

text.p: Russians captured all the gold at the European figure skating championships yet dire predictions still abound about the country's future in the sport.
Observers close to the Russian scene say success may be difficult to sustain because of a lack of coaches, money and adequate training facilities at home.
The observers point out that the current crop of champions were developed under the old Soviet set-up, where facilities and coaches were provided free by the state.

Singles champions Alexei Urmanov and Irina Slutskaya, pairs winners Marina Eltsova and Andrei Bushkov along with the triumphant ice dancers Oksana Gritschuk and Evgeny Platov all spent their formative years learning their trade in the former Soviet Union.

Since the break-up of the union in 1991, free ice time and state-paid coaches have largely evaporated in the new republics. Thus fewer children have entered the sport because their families lack the money to pay their expenses.
Several rinks have closed and many coaches have gone abroad. Those who have stayed have had to work for less money.
The established skaters, who now have opportunities to earn prize money that did not previously exist, can meet their costs and several have moved abroad to train.
Yet most of them are likely to leave the amateur scene after next year's Olympic and world championships.
A few coaches, such as the famed pairs trainer Tamara Moskvina, are still managing to produce good new prospects despite the deprivations.
Conditions are limited, she said last week. "But they are good enough if we work hard.
"We have just had to be move inventive in finding solutions."
Moskvina has masterminded the success of such pairs as Oleg Vasiliev and Elena Valova, and more recently Artur Dmitriev with Natalia Mishkutienok and later Oksana Kazakova.
Her forte is taking established skaters and moulding them into champions and she unveiled her newest medal contenders at the European championships, which ended on Saturday.

Elena Berezhnaia and Anton Sikharulidze came together only a year ago after Berezhnaia had recovered from an ugly injury caused when her former partner, Latvian Oleg Schliakov, caught her on the side of the head with his skate in practice.
They had both split with former partners but were already boyfriend and girlfriend when Moskvina brought them together on the ice.
"I told him 'This is your crystal vase. It was already broken and it's very easy to break again a thing that has been broken once, so be careful'," she said.
And Berezhnaia added during the week: "He is my boyfriend so he will take care of me."
Now the best in Europe have almost two months to prepare for the clashes with the North Americans and Chinese at the world championships in Lausanne in March.
Urmanov will keep practising his quadruple jump to take on Elvis Stojko of Canada and American Todd Eldredge.
Slutskaya will need improvement on her showing here to deal with American world champion Michelle Kwan and Chen Lu of China.
But Gritschuk and Platov should be able to look forward to another victory, probably over compatriots Anjelika Krylova and Oleg Ovsiannikov.
The only contenders joining the fray are Canadians Shae-Lynn Bourne and Victor Kraatz, third last year and likely to be fighting for silver or bronze again this time.
